correctness.rationale: Separately reconstructed the margins and mixed derivative. As x approaches 0 the powers stay bounded uniformly in y; as x approaches 1 the exponent tends to 1 and remains bounded away from zero, giving joint boundary continuity. For 0≤γ≤1, set s=1−x, t=1−xy and b=γs/x. The term −log t−s(1−t)/t is nonnegative on [s,1] by differentiation. The resulting lower bound on ∂x∂y C is s^b[1−γx−(γs/x)log s], strictly positive throughout the open square. Integrating on interior rectangles and passing to the continuous boundary proves two-increasingness. At x→1 with fixed y<1 the density tends to 1−γ−γ log(1−y). For γ>1 use y=0 and then continuity to obtain a negative interior rectangle; for γ<0 fix an interior y sufficiently near 1. For a≥1 the function u^a(−log u)/(1−u) is strictly increasing, as follows by factoring out u^(a−1) and differentiating the a=1 case. The parameter derivative is a positive prefactor times its difference at t and s; this proves the strict pointwise order and, by integration, strict Spearman ordering. Read VERIFICATION.md and check_int1.py without running the uploaded script; its sampled derivative and inequality tests are not used as a universal certificate.

value.rationale: Int1 is a published asymmetric dependence model without a tuning parameter. A natural nonlinear interpolation now admits exact validity limits and a strict dependence order without relying on sampled densities or assuming closure under exponent interpolation. The result tells users exactly which parameter values are available and how their dependence compares; no claims about fitting or estimation are needed.
